summary: Australia's PBAC uses an implicit ~50,000 AUD/QALY rule-of-thumb (~33,000 USD in 2024), with an empirical recommend/reject band spanning roughly 42,000-76,000 AUD/LY.
source_citation: Australian Prescriber, 'Economic evaluation of medicines' (https://australianprescriber.tg.org.au/articles/economic-evaluation-of-medicines.html); Wang et al., comparing ICERs to NICE/PBAC, ScienceDirect S1098301518302031 (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1098301518302031). Original ~50,000 AUD nominal x 0.66 USD/AUD = ~33,000 USD; rejection ~76,000 AUD/LY (~49,500 USD), near-certain accept ~42,000 AUD/LY (~27,700 USD).

summary: Canada's CADTH applies a de facto willingness-to-pay threshold of ~50,000 CAD/QALY (~36,500 USD in 2024) as the operative cost-effectiveness anchor for drug reimbursement.
source_citation: Skedgel et al., 'The impact of willingness-to-pay threshold on price reduction recommendations for oncology drugs: a review of CADTH assessments,' PubMed 38567953 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38567953/); Value in Health, 'CADTH's $50,000 Cost-Effectiveness Threshold: Fact or Fiction?' (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(16)32187-8/fulltext). Original 50,000 CAD nominal (~2021-2022) x 0.73 USD/CAD = ~36,500 USD (2024).

summary: Germany's IQWiG explicitly rejects any universal cost-per-QALY willingness-to-pay threshold, instead using an indication-specific efficiency-frontier method, so it supplies no single $/QALY anchor.
source_citation: Caro & Nord et al., 'The efficiency frontier approach to economic evaluation of health-care interventions,' ResearchGate 44699342 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/44699342_The_efficiency_frontier_approach_to_economic_evaluation_of_health-care_interventions); Gandjour 2015, Int J Health Plann Manage (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hpm.2247). Structural caveat: Germany provides no single anchor number.

summary: The Netherlands' Zorginstituut sets severity-tiered WTP reference values of 20,000/50,000/80,000 EUR/QALY by proportional shortfall, with the most-severe top tier of 80,000 EUR/QALY (~86,400 USD in 2024).
label_raw: Netherlands (ZIN) top tier 80,000 EUR/QALY; tiers 20,000/50,000/80,000 EUR
source_citation: Reckers-Droog et al. / 'Varying Willingness to Pay Based on Severity of Illness... Netherlands,' Value in Health S1098-3015(21)01690-9 (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(21)01690-9/fulltext). Established 2015; PS 0.10-0.40=20,000 EUR (~21,600 USD), PS 0.41-0.70=50,000 EUR (~54,000 USD), PS 0.71-1.00=80,000 EUR (~86,400 USD) at 1.08 USD/EUR. Top tier used as anchor value.

summary: Excluding the deprecated WHO multiplier and Germany's no-threshold method, the standard non-severity-adjusted cross-jurisdiction WTP-for-one-QALY midpoint sits at roughly 33,000-50,000 USD/QALY, with severity-weighted ceilings reaching ~86,000-94,000 USD/QALY.
label_raw: Cross-jurisdiction standard QALY midpoint ~33,000-50,000 USD; ceilings ~86,000-94,000 USD
source_citation: Calibration note synthesized from the qaly_intl jurisdiction set: high-income single-QALY anchors cluster as Thailand ~4,600; Australia ~33,000; Canada ~36,500; Netherlands ~22,000-86,000 (severity-scaled); Sweden ~19,000-94,000 (severity-scaled). Midpoint of the standard band (33,000-50,000) = ~41,500 USD used as money_value_usd2024.

summary: Sweden's TLV applies severity-tiered implied WTP up to ~750,000 SEK/QALY (high, ~70,500 USD) and ~1,000,000 SEK/QALY (very high, ~94,000 USD in 2024), with no statutory threshold and >2M SEK/QALY accepted for rare+severe cases.
source_citation: Svensson et al., 'Reimbursement Decisions for Pharmaceuticals in Sweden: Impact of Disease Severity and Cost Effectiveness,' PharmacoEconomics (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40273-015-0307-6); Quantify Research, 'How much is TLV willing to pay for a QALY in Sweden?' (2024) (https://quantifyresearch.com/2024/01/31/how-much-is-tlv-willing-to-pay-for-a-qaly-in-sweden/). Tiers at 0.094 USD/SEK: low 200k-250k (~19,000-23,500 USD), medium 500k-600k (~47,000-56,000 USD), high 750k (~70,500 USD), very high 1,000,000 (~94,000 USD). Very-high tier used as anchor value.

summary: Thailand's HITAP uses an explicit national WTP threshold of 160,000 THB/QALY (~4,560 USD in 2024, ~1.3x GDP per capita), above which ICERs trigger price negotiation.
source_citation: OHE, 'Around the World in HTAs: Thailand' (https://www.ohe.org/insights/around-the-world-in-htas-thailand/); Teerawattananon et al. / HITAP empirical study, ScienceDirect S221188372400090X (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S221188372400090X). Set 2013 (raised stepwise 100k pre-2010 -> 120k 2010 -> 160k 2013); 160,000 THB x 0.0285 USD/THB = ~4,560 USD (2024).

summary: The WHO-CHOICE / Commission on Macroeconomics and Health rule (2001) judged interventions cost-effective at 1x-3x GDP per capita per DALY averted, a generic global benchmark now deprecated as never rigorously derived.
label_raw: WHO-CHOICE / CMH 1x-3x GDP per capita per DALY (deprecated)
source_citation: Bertram et al., 'Understanding and improving the one and three times GDP per capita cost-effectiveness thresholds,' Health Policy and Planning 32(1):141 (https://academic.oup.com/heapol/article/32/1/141/2555408); WHO Bulletin, 'Thresholds for the cost-effectiveness of interventions: alternative approaches' (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4339959/). Multiplier of GDP/capita, not a fixed figure: at ~13,300 USD 2024 world GDP/capita, 1x-3x ~= 13,300-40,000 USD/DALY; LMIC like Thailand (~7,000 USD GDP/capita) 1x ~= 7,000 USD. money_value_usd2024 null because it scales with GDP per capita. Deprecated as a hard threshold.
